mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong demand for residential construction, which is a leading indicator of overall economic activity and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST rises in the prior month but S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that is likely to slow economic growth and reduce corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 12 months following the trigger condition, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a robust labor market and strong consumer spending, which together signal accelerating economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in PAYEMS and RSAFS occurs but the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% (YoY), the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing activity and economic expansion, which typically leads to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises in the prior month but S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In the 12 months following the trigger condition, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a stimulative economic environment that boosts consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and decline in FEDFUNDS occurs but the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A positive GDP growth surprise (GDPC1 > 0.5% quarter-over-quarter) in the latest reported quarter signals strong economic momentum, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 > 0.5% (QoQ), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances.
